Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test `testUnionOfVariableAndNode()` attempts to iterate over pointers returned by the XPath union expression `"$var | /MAIN/A"`. The error is an exception `JXPathException: Cannot compare pointers that do not belong to the same tree: '$var' and ''`.

Investigation of the stack trace and the relevant method `NodePointer.compareNodePointers` reveals that it recursively tries to compare the two node pointers by traversing their parent pointers until a shared ancestor is found or until it fails at depth 1. If at root level (depth 1) the two pointers are not equal, the method throws the reported exception.

This suggests that the two node pointers involved belong to different trees or roots. The failing pointers are likely the pointer for the variable `$var` (represented in code by `VariablePointer`) and the node pointer for the XML nodes `/MAIN/A`.

Examining `VariablePointer.equals` reveals it only returns true if the variables instance and the variable name are the same, indicating that a `VariablePointer` is specialized and does not share ancestry with XML node pointers.

Thus, the problem arises because the union operator `|` is attempting to unify pointers from two different trees or models: one set from a variable pointer (which does not have an XML node tree parentage), and the other from DOM node pointers (which belong to an XML document). When the comparison or ordering of results is internally attempted, the code crashes because it tries to compare pointers that do not belong to the same node tree.

This likely indicates that the union operator or pointer comparison logic does not correctly handle pointers originating from different models or variable pointers, failing to gracefully handle or unify them.

In summary, the code is failing because union iteration tries to compare and sort pointers from incompatible pointer types or trees without special accommodation. The comparison method `NodePointer.compareNodePointers` is not designed to handle the case where the two pointers belong to fundamentally different node spaces (variable vs XML node). This leads to the exception seen in the test scenario.

Next, to confirm this reasoning we could inspect the union iteration or union pointer comparison logic or the code that produces the pointers for `$var` and `/MAIN/A`.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
